newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Spain blocks Council resolution on state aid.
newsitem.headline: Spain blocks Council resolution on state aid.

text.p: European Union Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said on Thursday he would propose new rules aimed at increasing efficiency of state aid policies, despite Spain blocking an EU resolution on state aid.

Spain, winning some support from Greece and Portugal, declared at an Industry Council it could not accept a draft text designed to provide political support for a reform of state aid policies, EU officials said.
Its refusal appeared to reflect frustration that richer member states like Germany and France are able to give much more aid to their ailing industries than the poorer southern EU countries.
But Van Miert said ministers had endorsed his essential points and he would prepare legislation aimed at making state aid policies more transparent and efficient.
"The main objective has been achieved," he told reporters after a lengthy Council debate on the issue.
He said ministers welcomed the ideas put forward by the Commission and the Irish EU presidency to draw up proposals for new rules.
"So therefore I feel encouraged by this debate...and therefore the Commission is going to draft proposals and table them, I hope early next year," he said.

Van Miert said the proposals would aim at improving procedures in handling state aid policies, which would benefit all countries, while the Spanish objections had concerned the amounts of state aid being paid out in individual countries which he said was a separate debate.
"We need to distinguish between procedural improvements...then there is a separate issue, the amounts of aid," he said.

Instead of the full four-page resolution, the ministers could only agree on one paragraph which was issued as a "Council conclusion" taking note of the Commission's ideas on putting forward proposals regarding procedural rules.
The call for increased control and transparency in state aid rules come mostly from the EU's smaller states which cannot compete with their larger partners in the subsidy race.
Germany and France are seen as pouring the most state money into their industries.

The draft resolution urged the Commission to develop a user-friendly rule book on state aid control and to establish a register of cases which have been dealt with to allow for a better understanding of the situation.

The Commission said in its 1995 report on competition policy that the average annual aid for the Union as a whole was 94 billion European currency units, or 1.9 percent of the bloc's gross domestic product.
Although there are no exact figures, industry and Commission officials fear that the actual level of aid paid has increased considerably since the reunification of Germany in 1990.
